newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BOURSE RALLY IS SUSTAINABLE- ING BARINGS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BOURSE RALLY IS SUSTAINABLE- ING BARINGS.

text.p: Better Greek economic fundamentals, political maturity with a commitment to EU convergence, a high trading volume and lively participation by retailers make the stock market rally sustainable, said ING Barings.
"We expect this rally to be more sustainable...for the three following reasons: The fundamental story behind it is not speculative in nature." said ING Barings in its flash report.
"We are looking forward to a more lively participation of domestic investors."
The rally was not characterised by an abnormally high and therefore unsustainable volume, said Barings in citing the third reason.

The report said the stock market rally reflected an upgrading of Greece's economy and politics in investors' minds demonstrated by a tight 1997 budget, falling inflation and interest rates and the government's tough stance against various interest groups.
"Retail investors are aggressively seeking higher yields while life insurance funds are finding it increasingly hard to achieve their mandatory minimum return of 5.0 percent," it said.
These reasons make the recent stock market rally much different from the past short-lived rallies of June 1990, March 1991 and January 1994, it added.
But Barings said investment flows into the Mediterranean region which depend largely on the course of the $ would play an important role in determining the sustainability of the rally.

"...The Athens stock exchange appears to have been correlated with the $ since late 1991," said the report written by analyst Yannis Protopapadakis. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
